citations.narrative:
APHIS was unable to review disposition records for two chinchillas that had been sold, as well as acquisition records for
three hedgehogs and two parakeets that were not noted on the previous inspection report, as these records were not
available at the time of the inspection. Failure to maintain accurate acquisition of disposition records of animals on hand
prevents APHIS officials from verifying that these activities are compliant with the Animal Welfare Act. The facility must
ensure that it makes, maintains, and keeps records or forms which fully and correctly disclose all required information
concerning animals purchased or otherwise acquired, owned, held, leased, or otherwise in his or her possession or under
his or her control, or which is transported, sold, euthanized, or otherwise disposed of by the facility. The licensee filled out
acquisition and disposition records for these animals at the time of the inspection.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
